survivingClaim:
No lower bound is obtained; precise obstruction in corrected form. For a finite set S of primes and smooth compactly supported one-sided tests, M_S = prod(1-U_p) maps the class into itself with range of infinite codimension (not onto). Every test is nevertheless a simultaneous L^2 and Q limit of jointly S-primitive tests (referee repair, classical zero-free region). So inf Q/norm^2 over jointly primitive tests equals the infimum over all tests of the class: the primitive restriction neither helps nor costs, for zeta and for controls with zeros in a comparable region. That this bound is "P10 itself" is not established, because P10 is proved on a different test class.

The Gram matrix of dilations does not contain the function's coefficients. It replaces the divergent product by about log P only in mean over height; the sup over all heights is the full product, attained at tau = 0. All-prime Hecke sums Zw lie in the radical of the zero sum (known, P12). Lemma 2 (single-lag collapse on p-primitive tests) and the y_z defect formulas of Lemma 5 are correct identities.

Measured (float64): the sign of the minimum eigenvalue is unchanged by the primitive restriction for zeta, DH, Liouville twist, random signs, E_a and T-NR. DH is positive to rounding on a band without off-line zeros. Flags: R1 = R2 = R3 = R4 = false.
obstruction: For a finite set S of primes, jointly S-primitive tests are dense (L^2 and Q) in the test class, so the infimum of Q/norm^2 over primitive tests equals the infimum over all tests: the restriction neither helps nor costs. The Gram matrix of dilations does not contain the function's coefficients. All-prime Hecke sums lie in the radical of the zero sum. Referee does not hold the result as written (Lemma 3(a) domain: inverse of M_S does not preserve compact support; 'this is P10 itself' not established).
controlsThatDefeat: DH, Liouville twist, random signs, E_a, T-NR: sign of the minimum eigenvalue unchanged by the primitive restriction (float64, measured)
lesson: Hecke/Moebius operators are translation multipliers with no zeros in the open strip, so restricting a translation-invariant form (Weil/Q_L) to primitive tests is a congruence and changes nothing; the orthogonalisation step is function-independent. Any multiplicative mechanism must act where the cutoff fails to commute with Hecke (window defect), and that formula is also kernel-independent. Reusable tool: plib.py computes Q_L from primes alone in an orthonormal basis (Loewner form) for zeta and four controls, validated against zero sums to 1e-12.
followUp: None on this route. The only surviving adjacent question is OPEN and of largest-value type: the size of sum over zeros of |zeta_S(1/2+i gamma)|^2 |W(i gamma)|^2 against the norm of Z_S w as S grows (partial Euler products sampled at zeros). The result needs a referee pass on Lemmas 3-5 before the map row is closed.
